A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ClinRaGen despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original diagnosis experiments, rationale evaluations by GPT-4 and humans, component ablations, and backbone/teacher comparisons on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised Qwen results in Appendix Table 6.

M1.justification: Knowledge retrieval, rationale generation, knowledge-augmented attention and the three distillation phases remain unchanged, including their inputs and objectives. The added explanation about avoiding clinically irrelevant tokens does not introduce a different mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV for diagnosis of 25 disease phenotypes and multimodal rationale generation. The backbone and teacher variations in Table 6 already appear in v2; they do not introduce new task or population coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods are unchanged. However, Table 6 replaces the label w/o LAB&KNOW with Clinical-COT, described as single-modal CoT distillation. Matching Flan-T5 and OPT scores suggest relabeling, but the PDFs do not establish whether this denotes the same ablation or a different implemented comparator.

E3.justification: The reported dataset sizes, 4:1 train/test split, preprocessing, model configurations, diagnosis metrics, five-shot prompting, and rationale-evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged. No revised experimental setting is documented to explain the changed Qwen scores.

E4.justification: Table 6 revises the Qwen evidence within the existing backbone/teacher ablation study. Its experimental questions and model coverage remain the same. The component-removal ablations in Table 2, efficiency analysis and Figure 7 case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both report five-run averages and t-tests at p < 0.05. Table 1's parenthetical variability entries and the human-evaluation agreement values of 0.637 and 0.608 remain identical. No new uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: All Qwen result entries in Table 6 change. For example, ChatGPT-distilled ClinRaGen's MIMIC-III micro/macro F1 changes from 0.5412/0.5011 to 0.6207/0.5688; MIMIC-IV changes from 0.5316/0.4997 to 0.6332/0.6105. Tables 1–3, the other backbones, and BLEU/BERTScore results remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether the revisions reflect corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, including the knowledge-vocabulary construction, attention expression and training objectives, are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The new mechanism and architecture explanations are informal interpretations.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims of accurate, efficient, LLM-comparable multimodal reasoning remain the same. v4 adds bias mitigation to the conclusion, but this claim already appears in v2's case discussion and Appendix A.8. The shorter title does not change the research scope.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the separate Flan-T5 and ChatGPT selection discussions with interpretations of decoder-only gains, encoder-decoder performance and similarity across teachers in Appendix A.6. It also explains attention as redirecting focus from frequent irrelevant tokens. The detailed appendix leakage argument is removed, although the main-text leakage claim and substantive limitations remain.

D1.justification: The model-access reference changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository; its availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Prompt descriptions are generalized from ChatGPT to teacher LLMs. The implementation hyperparameters, software, hardware and time-series processing details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations concerning attention, CoT datasets, multimodal distillation, LLM-as-a-judge and Qwen, while removing the T5 and GPT-2 references associated with the replaced selection discussion. It also substitutes the Llama 2 report for the original Llama reference. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 changes the title, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments and makes scattered grammar and terminology corrections. It moves the BLEU/BERTScore subsection from Appendix A.6 to Section 4.4 and replaces the final model-selection subsections with a combined discussion. Most of the narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 receive limited label and alignment refinements. Table 6 gains a Method column, reordered paired rows and bold highlighting. The unchanged BLEU/BERTScore table moves into the main text, while other floats shift position. No new figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: v4 improves prose, diagram labels and visibility of the rationale metrics. However, Table 6's score revisions and comparator relabeling are unexplained. The new teacher-stability interpretation also accompanies Qwen MIMIC-IV macro F1 values of 0.6105/0.5583 for ChatGPT/DeepSeek, compared with v2's 0.4997/0.4991. These unresolved evidence and interpretation issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the presentation gains.
